info.title: Queue Metrics API
info.description:
Retrieve real-time operational metrics for queues in the Avaya Infinity contact center platform — including agent availability, engagement wait counts, and queue occupancy. Designed for external integrations such as routing systems, orchestration platforms, and wallboard/reporting tools that need live queue data.

## Endpoints

### Query Queue Metrics

`POST /queue-metrics`

Returns current metrics for a specific queue and communication channel.

## Getting Started

### Find Your Customer Subdomain

Your subdomain is found in your Avaya Infinity portal URL and is required for all API calls.

**Example:** If your portal URL is:

```
https://core.avaya1234.ec.avayacloud.com/app/core-config-ui/
```

Your subdomain is: **`avaya1234`**

All API requests use this base URL format:

```
https://core.{customerId}.ec.avayacloud.com/api/matching-extensions/v1/...
```

### Authentication

All endpoints require a Bearer token obtained via the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow.

1. **Request credentials from Avaya Support** — you will need a `client_id` and `client_secret` provisioned with the **`QUEUE_METRICS`** scope. This is not self-serve and requires raising a request with Avaya Support.
2. Use your `client_id` and `client_secret` to request a token:

```
POST https://core.{customerId}.ec.avayacloud.com/auth/realms/avaya/protocol/openid-connect/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<your_client_id>&client_secret=<your_client_secret>&scope=QUEUE_METRICS
```

3. Include the returned `access_token` in all requests:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

For full authentication instructions, see [How to Authenticate with Avaya Infinity APIs](https://developers.avayacloud.com/avaya-infinity/docs/how-to-authenticate-with-avaya-infinitytm-apis).

### Working with Queue IDs and Tags

The `queueId` field accepts the unique identifier of the queue — not its display name. Queue IDs can be found in the Avaya Infinity portal or retrieved via the Queue Management API.

Optionally, filter metrics further by providing one or more tag IDs in the `tags` field. Tags are comma-separated and can be found in the portal alongside queue configuration. Metrics returned will reflect only engagements and agents matching both the queue and the specified tags.

**Example with tags:**

```json
{
  "commType": "voice",
  "queueId": "003d010826307dd6630992437c",
  "tags": "006d0110160d0bea955297d80e, 006d01101602a2f055c1a03dcb"
}
```

### Important Notes

* Metrics are real-time — each request returns the current state of the queue at the time of the call.
* If no engagements are currently waiting, `oldestEngagementWaiting` returns an empty string and `queueOccupancy` returns `0`.
* The `commType` field must match an active channel configured on the queue. Querying an inactive or unconfigured channel will return a 404.
* This API is rate limited to **600 requests per minute** per client credential.
* The account/tenant is automatically derived from your Bearer token — no separate account identifier is required in the request.

tags.name: Queue Metrics
tags.description: Real-time metrics for queues, including agent availability, wait counts, and occupancy.

post.description:
Returns real-time metrics for a specific queue and communication channel, including agent counts, engagement wait counts, queue occupancy, and the timestamp of the oldest waiting engagement.

Both `commType` and `queueId` are required. Optionally include `tags` to filter metrics to a specific tag subset within the queue.

## Finding Your Customer Subdomain

Your subdomain is found in your Avaya Infinity portal URL and is required for all API calls.

**Example:** If your portal URL is:

```
https://core.avaya1234.ec.avayacloud.com/app/core-config-ui/
```

Your subdomain is: **`avaya1234`**

**To use this API:**

1. **Find your subdomain** from your Infinity portal URL (as shown above)
2. **Get your Bearer token** using the `QUEUE_METRICS` client credential (see Authentication below)
3. **In the API explorer on the right:**
   * Click on `{customerId}` in the URL field and replace it with your actual subdomain
   * Paste your Bearer token in the Credentials section
   * Fill out the Body Parameters with your `commType` and `queueId`

## Authentication

This endpoint requires a valid OAuth 2.0 Bearer token. To use this API, you will need a `client_id` and `client_secret` provisioned with the **`QUEUE_METRICS`** scope — this is not self-serve and requires raising a request with Avaya Support.

Once you have your credentials, use the client credentials flow to obtain a token:

```
POST https://core.{customerId}.ec.avayacloud.com/auth/realms/avaya/protocol/openid-connect/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<your_client_id>&client_secret=<your_client_secret>&scope=QUEUE_METRICS
```

Include the returned token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header of each request.

For full authentication instructions, see [How to Authenticate with Avaya Infinity APIs](https://developers.avayacloud.com/avaya-infinity/docs/how-to-authenticate-with-avaya-infinitytm-apis).

## Working with Queue IDs and Tags

The `queueId` field accepts the unique identifier of the queue — not its display name. Queue IDs can be found in the Avaya Infinity portal or retrieved via the Queue Management API.

Optionally, filter metrics further by providing one or more tag IDs in the `tags` field. When provided, metrics are scoped to only engagements and agents matching both the queue and the specified tags.

**Supported tag formats:**

```
Single tag:       "006d0110160d0bea955297d80e"
Comma-separated:  "006d0110160d0bea955297d80e, 006d01101602a2f055c1a03dcb"
Array notation:   "[006d0110160d0bea955297d80e, 006d01101602a2f055c1a03dcb]"
```

## Important Notes

* Metrics are real-time — each request returns the current state of the queue at the time of the call.
* If no engagements are currently waiting, `oldestEngagementWaiting` returns an empty string and `queueOccupancy` returns `0`.
* If an unrecognized or non-existent `queueId` is provided, the API returns a `200` with all metrics zeroed out rather than a `404`.
* The `commType` field must match an active channel configured on the queue.
* The account/tenant is automatically derived from your Bearer token — no separate account identifier is required in the request.

## DOS Protection & Rate Limiting

* This endpoint is rate limited to 600 requests per minute per client credential.

## Security Implementation Guidelines

* Never expose your `client_secret` or Bearer token to client-side applications.
* Implement proper error handling — avoid surfacing internal error details to end users.

basicQuery.summary: Query metrics for a voice queue

queryWithTags.summary: Query metrics for a chat queue filtered by tags

voiceQueueMetrics.summary: Voice queue with active agents and waiting engagements

emptyQueue.summary: Queue with no activity, or unrecognized queue ID — both return zeroed metrics

400.description: Bad request — missing or malformed required fields.

malformedBody.summary: Request body could not be parsed

401.description: Missing or invalid Bearer token. Note that in practice, requests made without a valid token may receive a `302` redirect response at the gateway level rather than a `401` JSON error. Ensure your HTTP client does not automatically follow redirects when an unexpected `302` is received — this is an indicator of a missing or expired token.

403.description: Forbidden — token is valid but does not have the `QUEUE_METRICS` scope.

404.description: Returned when a timeout occurs waiting for initial metrics. Note that providing an unrecognized or non-existent `queueId` does **not** return a 404 — the API returns a `200` with all metrics fields zeroed out in that case.

timeout.summary: Timed out waiting for initial metrics

503.description: Service temporarily unavailable. Retry after a short delay.

example.error: service is not ready: stream not connected

To use this API, you will need a `client_id` and `client_secret` provisioned with the **`QUEUE_METRICS`** scope. This is not self-serve — raise a request with Avaya Support to obtain credentials.

Once provisioned, request a token:

```
POST https://core.{customerId}.ec.avayacloud.com/auth/realms/avaya/protocol/openid-connect/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<your_client_id>&client_secret=<your_client_secret>&scope=QUEUE_METRICS
```

Include the returned token as: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`

MetricsType.description: The internal type of the metrics query. For queue-based queries via this API, this will always be `attribute`.

QueueMetricsQueryRequest.description: Request body for querying real-time metrics for a specific queue and channel.

commType.description:
The communication channel to query metrics for. Must match a channel actively configured on the target queue.

Valid values: `voice`, `chat`, `email`

queueId.description: The unique identifier of the queue to query. Queue IDs can be found in the Avaya Infinity portal or via the Queue Management API.

tags.description:
Optional. One or more tag IDs to filter metrics to a specific subset of agents and engagements within the queue. When provided, metrics are scoped to only those matching all specified tags.

Supported formats:
- Single tag: `"006d0110160d0bea955297d80e"`
- Comma-separated: `"006d0110160d0bea955297d80e, 006d01101602a2f055c1a03dcb"`
- Array notation: `"[006d0110160d0bea955297d80e, 006d01101602a2f055c1a03dcb]"`

MetricsResponse.description: Real-time metrics snapshot for the requested queue and channel.

channel.description: The communication channel these metrics apply to.

accountId.description: The account/tenant identifier derived from the Bearer token.

agentStaffedCount.description: Total number of agents currently logged in and assigned to this queue.

agentReadyCount.description: Number of agents in a Ready state and available to handle engagements.

agentBusyCount.description: Number of agents currently handling an active engagement.

waitingEngagementCount.description: Number of engagements currently waiting in queue to be assigned to an agent.

processingEngagementCount.description: Number of engagements currently being handled by an agent (in progress).

queueOccupancy.description: Queue occupancy rate as a decimal between 0 and 1 (e.g., `0.75` means 75% occupied). Returns `0` when no engagements are waiting or in progress.

oldestEngagementWaiting.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601) of the oldest engagement currently waiting in queue. Returns an empty string if no engagements are waiting.

timestamp.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601) indicating when this metrics snapshot was collected.

attributes.description: The attribute values used to resolve these metrics, in `queue:{queueId}` and `tag:{tagId}` format.

error.description: A message describing what went wrong.
